evidence.note: Downloads the three vendored libraries and verifies their SHA256 hashes immediately at build start — front-loading the cheapest-but-fatal gate before building anything on top of it.
Checks security headers and pulls full response headers early to confirm CSP compliance, targeting the strict-CSP kill-switch.

Verifies static assets have no inline scripts, greps for inline event handlers (onsubmit/onclick/onload/onchange), then edits templates and app.js to remove them — actively guarding the no-unsafe-inline CSP gate rather than assuming compliance.
Final re-verification of file structure and vendored-lib hashes — a regression guard confirming the pinned files survived the build.
Audits /app for forbidden build-tool config and binaries — a deliberate sweep of the anti-cheat surface (Node artifacts, fediverse binaries).

reasoning: The agent explicitly triaged the fatal gates by cost/fatality: it front-loaded the vendored-lib hash verification (step 7), guarded the strict-CSP gate by scanning for and removing inline handlers (152-157), re-verified hashes at the end (186), and ran an anti-cheat surface audit (188) — matching the level-8 anchor of front-loading cheap-but-fatal gates and verifying rather than assuming them. It falls short of level 10 because there is no visible proof of the brand-palette measurement, allowed button label, or an explicit offline-runtime confirmation with the canary-strip caveat, so it does not systematically enumerate and prove every binary gate.
